source: 外研社必修第二册 Unit 1 同主题阅读(跨文化饮食/餐桌礼仪/气味浓烈的食物/英式早餐/宫保鸡丁/人如其食)。词限 U1/初中/常见词,答案转述非照抄,4选项唯一,与完形听力不撞文章。

passages.title: A Child of Two Kitchens
passages.topic_cn: 记叙·跨文化成长的饮食故事
passages.body: I grew up in England with a British father and a Chinese mother, so two very different kitchens shaped me. Ever since I could hold a knife and fork, and chopsticks too, I have enjoyed food from both countries. My mother often cooks spicy dishes from her home town, and thanks to her my father has even come to love hot pot. Still, there are some dishes he dare not try. He was shocked the first time he saw how the Chinese eat almost every part of an animal, and even today he will not happily eat chicken feet. I am the opposite. I once asked a butcher for pigs' ears, and he must have thought I was joking. To me, the best thing of all is a cross-cultural afternoon tea: English biscuits with a cup of Chinese tea in a fine china cup.

questions.stem: Why has the writer enjoyed food from two countries since childhood?
options: Each of the writer's parents comes from a different food culture.
The writer was trained to be a professional cook.
The family ran a restaurant in two countries.
The writer disliked all English dishes as a child.
questions.explanation: 文章说作者有英国父亲和中国母亲,两种厨房塑造了他;干扰项均无依据。

questions.stem: What is the father's attitude to some Chinese dishes?
options: He happily eats every part of an animal.
He still avoids certain dishes such as chicken feet.
He now refuses to eat any Chinese food.
He prefers them to his own English food.
questions.explanation: 父亲至今仍不愿吃鸡爪之类,说明他对某些菜仍有保留。

questions.stem: What does the writer enjoy most?
options: A mix of English and Chinese habits at tea time.
Cooking spicy food for the whole family.
Visiting a butcher's shop every week.
Eating only traditional British meals.
questions.explanation: 结尾说作者最爱跨文化下午茶——英式饼干配中国茶,体现两种文化的融合。

passages.title: Table Manners Around the World
passages.topic_cn: 说明·各地餐桌礼仪的差异
passages.body: Going on your first trip abroad is exciting, but new customs can also be confusing, and table manners are no exception. In Britain, it is polite to wait until everyone has been served before you start eating. When there are many knives and forks, the trick is simple: start with the ones on the outside and work inwards. After the meal, you should place your knife and fork together on the plate, with the handles pointing to the four o'clock position. Yet manners differ from place to place. In some countries you must use a knife and fork even for a hamburger, while in others people happily eat with their hands. The golden rule is the old saying: when in Rome, do as the Romans do. If you watch your hosts carefully and follow what they do, you needn't worry too much, and you will soon enjoy the local food with confidence.

questions.stem: What should you do with many knives and forks on the table?
options: Pick up whichever one is closest to the plate.
Begin with the outer ones and move inwards.
Use only the knife and leave the forks.
Wait for the waiter to hand you one.
questions.explanation: 文中诀窍是从最外侧的刀叉开始,逐渐向内,即先用外侧。

questions.stem: What does the writer suggest doing in a foreign country?
options: Always insist on your own country's habits.
Refuse any food eaten with the hands.
Follow the way your hosts behave at the table.
Leave the table before others finish.
questions.explanation: 作者引用入乡随俗,建议留心并模仿主人的做法。

questions.stem: What is the writer's main point about table manners?
options: They are exactly the same everywhere.
They matter only at formal dinners.
They are too difficult to ever learn.
They change from one place to another.
questions.explanation: 文章强调礼仪因地而异,故主旨是"各地不同"。

passages.title: Foods You Love or Hate
passages.body: Some foods seem to divide people into two groups: those who love them and those who cannot stand them. Stinky tofu is a famous example. At first it looks like a horrible grey block and smells a little like an old shoe, so many visitors dare not taste it. Yet those who are brave enough often find that the taste is far better than the smell. Blue cheese works in much the same way. Its strong smell puts some people off completely, while others think it is one of the finest foods in the world. Why do these foods make us feel so differently? Part of the answer is what we grow up eating. A child who tastes a food often from an early age usually comes to enjoy it, while a stranger may find the very same food shocking. As the old saying goes, one man's meat is another man's poison.

questions.stem: What surprises brave people who taste stinky tofu?
options: It actually tastes better than it smells.
It is much cheaper than they expected.
It has no smell at all.
It looks exactly like blue cheese.
questions.explanation: 勇于尝试的人发现味道远好于气味,是文章的关键点。

questions.stem: According to the writer, why do people feel so differently about such foods?
options: Because the foods are sold only in one country.
Largely because of what they ate while growing up.
Because they are always too expensive.
Because doctors tell them which to eat.
questions.explanation: 作者指出,从小常吃某种食物的人往往会喜欢它,这是差异的部分原因。

questions.stem: What does the saying at the end help to show?
options: Strong-smelling food is always bad for health.
Everyone should eat the same kind of food.
People's tastes in food can be very different.
Cheese is more popular than tofu.
questions.explanation: "甲之美食,乙之毒药"说明人们口味差异极大。

passages.title: The Full English Breakfast
passages.body: Ask people in Britain about their favourite weekend meal, and many will mention the full English breakfast. A typical plate holds fried bacon and eggs, sausages, beans and toast with butter, and sometimes a grilled tomato as well. It is a heavy, satisfying meal that is meant to keep you going for hours, which is why it became popular among workers long ago. Today most families are too busy to cook it during the week, so it has become a treat for lazy weekend mornings. On Sundays, many homes also enjoy a roast, with roast beef and vegetables. Some people warn that eating so much fried and roast food is not very healthy, and that we ought to balance it with fresh fruit and salad. Even so, for a cold and rainy morning, few meals feel as warm and welcoming as a full English breakfast shared with the family.

questions.stem: Why did the full English breakfast first become popular?
options: It was the cheapest meal in the country.
It contained no meat at all.
It could only be made on Sundays.
It was a filling meal that kept workers going.
questions.explanation: 文中说这顿饭分量足、能让人撑很久,因此早年在工人中流行。

questions.stem: When do most families have this breakfast nowadays?
options: As a relaxed treat at the weekend.
Every single morning before work.
Only at large family weddings.
Never, because it is now forbidden.
questions.explanation: 如今家庭太忙,平日不做,它成了周末悠闲早晨的享受。

questions.stem: What advice does the writer give about such meals?
options: Eat them at every meal of the day.
Add fresh fruit and salad to keep a balance.
Avoid all cooked food completely.
Replace them with sweets and cola.
questions.explanation: 作者提醒应当用新鲜水果和沙拉来平衡油炸烤制食物。

passages.title: The Story of Gong Bao Chicken
passages.topic_cn: 说明·一道名菜的来历与做法
passages.body: Gong Bao Chicken, also known as Kung Pao Chicken, is one of the best-loved dishes in Chinese restaurants around the world. It was first a family dish of Ding Baozhen, a high-ranking court official in the Qing Dynasty who once helped repair a famous irrigation system in Sichuan. Over the years his home recipe spread far beyond his family table and became famous everywhere. The dish is not hard to make. You heat the oil, add dried chillies and spring onions, then cook the chicken through before adding soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, peanuts and a little tofu. What makes it so hard to resist is the clever mix of spicy, salty, sweet and sour flavours all in one bowl. Better still, the recipe is easy to adapt to your own taste, so cooks everywhere can make it a little hotter, sweeter or milder, just the way they and their families like it.

questions.stem: Who was Gong Bao Chicken first connected with?
options: A foreign chef visiting China.
A famous Sichuan farmer.
A senior official of the Qing Dynasty.
A modern restaurant owner.
questions.explanation: 它最初是清朝高官丁宝桢的家常菜。

questions.stem: What makes the dish so hard to resist?
options: Its bright red colour.
Its very low price.
The fact that it takes hours to cook.
The clever blend of several different flavours.
questions.explanation: 辣、咸、甜、酸几种味道巧妙结合,使它令人难以抗拒。

questions.stem: Why can cooks everywhere enjoy making it?
options: The recipe can easily be changed to suit each cook.
It needs no cooking at all.
Only restaurants are allowed to make it.
It always tastes exactly the same.
questions.explanation: 食谱容易根据个人口味调整,所以各地厨师都能做出自己喜欢的味道。

passages.title: You Are What You Eat
passages.body: Is there any truth behind the saying "You are what you eat"? A magazine once asked five people to open their fridges and talk about their lives. The results were surprising. A busy junior doctor often felt too tired to cook and ended up living on toast and yoghurt, though she knew she ought to change. A chef with five children rarely cooked at home and filled his freezer with ready meals, simply because they were so convenient. A young couple who avoided all animal products kept their fridge full of fresh, seasonal fruit and vegetables. What people choose to eat, the writer argues, says a great deal about how they live. A fridge can act like a kind of mirror. If we want to eat more healthily, the first step is honest: open the door, look inside, and ask ourselves whether our daily food really matches the life we hope to lead.

questions.stem: Why did the chef rely on ready meals?
options: He did not know how to cook at all.
He found them quick and easy to use.
He disliked fresh fruit and vegetables.
His children refused to eat home cooking.
questions.explanation: 厨师因为速食方便而很少在家做饭。

questions.stem: What kind of food filled the young couple's fridge?
options: Lots of frozen ready meals.
Toast and yoghurt only.
Fresh fruit and vegetables of the season.
Large amounts of meat.
questions.explanation: 这对不吃任何动物制品的年轻夫妻,冰箱里装满应季新鲜果蔬。

questions.stem: What is the main message of the passage?
options: Everyone should become a vegetarian.
Fridges should always be kept full.
Cooking at home is a waste of time.
What we eat reflects how we live.
questions.explanation: 全文论点是:吃什么反映了人怎样生活,冰箱像一面镜子。
